transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been experiencing constant, uncontrollable worry about almost everything in my life, from my job to my family and finances. This has been going on for over two years now, and it has just become completely overwhelming.
Do you also experience physical symptoms like restlessness, fatigue, or muscle tension along with the worry?

Yes, I definitely experience a lot of muscle tension and fatigue. My neck and shoulders are constantly knotted and stiff, and I often catch myself clenching my jaw. My whole body just feels achy, tight, and completely exhausted most of the time.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "duration and functional impairment",
  "question": "How has this worry and the physical tension affected your daily life, such as your work or relationships?"

It has had a huge impact on my daily life. At work, the constant worries and physical aches make it incredibly hard to focus, and my mind often just goes blank. In my relationships, the physical tension and exhaustion have worn my patience so thin that I've become really snappy and easily frustrated over minor things.
Do you also have trouble sleeping, such as difficulty falling or staying asleep, or waking up too early?
Actually, my sleep is generally fine. I don't really have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep.

These are all hallmark features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. The absence of sleep disturbance does not rule it out, as sleep issues are not required for diagnosis. No new symptoms suggesting an alternative diagnosis have emerged.
